summary: A harness.usage context_occupancy reading that says how full the window is replicates when it moves 5 or more points of the window from the replicated reading, on a compaction or model change, or when the seat ends, instead of every five minutes and at every turn end; the seat's host still reads its newest occupancy

replay.detail: Fewer harness.usage claims are written. A context_occupancy reading with context_used_percent, or with context_used_tokens and context_window_tokens, stays pending in the host's local observation log unless it is the slot's first reading, is at least 5 points of the window from the slot's replicated reading, or changes compactions or model. A pending reading replicates when the seat reports ended or indeterminate, or when its step is completed, failed or released; a reading after the seat ended, or from a replaced incarnation, replicates at once. Turn ends, resting re-stamps and the five-minute interval no longer replicate it. Readings that don't say how full the window is, and seats that never report a state, keep the existing rules. Old claims are untouched.

schema.detail: No schema change: pending occupancy uses the existing local_latest_slots.pending_local_id.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Part of contract C2's step (approved). On the seat's host, the agent, mission and run cards fold the pending occupancy with its own observed time, so the context number and its freshness stay exact. On other members a card's occupancy is within 5 points of the window and its observed time is the last replicated reading's. Compactions replicate at once everywhere. No claim kind, field, wire or CLI shape changes; an older node keeps its old schedule, and every node reads both.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting replicates each pending occupancy reading at its seat's next turn end or interval; the readings stay in each host's local observation log meanwhile.
